doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: First jazz playing and learning tunes from his father's sheet music
summary: Began real jazz around 1940-42, learned songs like Sweet Lorraine from sheet music his father bought, adding chord changes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What can you say about that? So you got out of, late 1930s, no, you said you were born in 1925. Okay. So late 1930s, early 1940s, you had to make a decision about what you were going to do.

Well let’s see. I started studying music in ’25 — about 1930 I started classical music. And I was playing, you know, playing around. But I didn’t get to play any jazz, anything noteworthy until about 1940, ’42. And when I started it’s like, guys would tell me about — thinking about the chord man, “You’re not playing the right chords,” you know, saying “you play beautiful runs and things, but you’re just not playing the right chords. It’s sort of off, and this whole thing’s sort of off.” And I said, “Okay, man, I’ll try to study and make a different arrangement.”
Can you name a few of the tunes that you might have been playing back then?
Oh boy. I don’t know. “Sweet Lorraine.” “You Can’t Give Me Anything but Love,” Boy.
And did you have a lead sheet? Like melody and chords? How did you learn the songs?

Well what I used to depend on, my father, he would go in the music store. And if he heard tunes on the radio, he would buy them and bring them home for me. And I would pick out ones that I liked and play them, and then figure out what I was going to change. And he would tell me, say “Listen, don’t try to change the man’s melody.” I said, “No I’m not going to change his melody I’m just going to add to the chord changes.”
That’s good. That’s good. Using your ears. Yeah.
Yeah. It wasn’t easy. It took quite a little while to cover that, but to do it especially while you’re playing, to do it by playing.
